steps: Paso 1: Test de primer encendido seguro con fuente de laboratorio limitada a 150 mA para proteger contra cortocircuitos accidentales.
Paso 2: Ejecución de un escáner de bus (ej. I2C Scanner) para verificar que el periférico responde en su dirección hex esperada.
Paso 3: Protocolo de reposo estático (Zero-Motion Calibration): Mantener el dispositivo inmóvil sobre una superficie nivelada durante 5 segundos para calcular y restar el sesgo estático (bias).
Paso 4: Validación de rango dinámico: Aplicar estímulos conocidos y verificar mediante el Serial Plotter que la señal responde sin saturación ni ruido espurio.
Paso 5: Calibración de tiempo muerto y seguridad de desconexión (Failsafe timeout): Comprobar que el sistema entra en modo seguro si se interrumpe la comunicación por más de 100 ms.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: El microcontrolador no detecta el módulo o el bus se congela aleatoriamente.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Ausencia de resistencias pull-up adecuadas o cableado demasiado largo con capacitancia parasita > 400 pF.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Añadir resistencias pull-up externas de 2.2 kΩ a 4.7 kΩ entre las líneas SDA/SCL y el riel de 3.3V, y acortar los cables a menos de 10 cm.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicios esporádicos del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al arrancar actuadores o transmisores.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Caída brusca de tensión provocada por el pico de corriente de arranque (inrush current) del periférico.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Soldar un condensador electrolítico de baja ESR de 470 µF a 1000 µF en paralelo con el riel de potencia y alimentar la etapa de potencia mediante una fuente independiente con masa común.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Ruido excesivo o deriva continua en la señal adquirida.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento electromagnético procedente de motores o falta de filtrado cerámico de alta frecuencia en la alimentación.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Colocar un condensador cerámico SMD de 100 nF lo más cerca posible de los pines VDD y GND del sensor, y habilitar un filtro paso bajo digital (DLPF) en el firmware.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Sobrecalentamiento del regulador de voltaje LDO o del circuito integrado.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Disipación de potencia excesiva por caída de tensión elevada (ej. alimentar un chip de 3.3V desde 12V a través de un regulador lineal).
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Reemplazar el LDO lineal por un convertidor reductor conmutado (Buck DC-DC) de alta eficiencia o añadir un disipador de aluminio.

officialData.whyThisMatters: A large steel object — a vehicle, a pipe, a ship — distorts the Earth’s magnetic field around it, and a sensitive magnetometer can detect that distortion from a distance, with no contact and no emission. This is magnetic anomaly detection (MAD), used in defense for submarine hunting and mine detection, and in the civilian world for archaeology, geophysics, and utility locating. Building one teaches you to pull a tiny anomaly out of a large, noisy background field — a purely passive sensing skill with the same signal-in-noise flavour as the RF work, but in the magnetic domain. defense signals — a Build List field guide 8 / 17 --- PAGE 9 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand magnetometry (fluxgate and magnetoresistive sensors), the Earth’s field as a baseline, gradiometry to cancel common-mode drift, calibration, and anomaly detection against a noisy background. Passive magnetic sensing is used across defense, geophysics, and navigation.
officialData.jobMapping: magnetic sensing and geophysical engineering — defense sensor, survey, navigation, and instrumentation teams.

howItWorks.title: BUILD NOTE A single magnetometer drifts with temperature and Earth-field changes. Use two identical sensors as a gradiometer — subtracting one from the other cancels the common background and leaves the local anomaly, the trick that makes real MAD work. The Earth’s field as baseline
howItWorks.description: The geomagnetic field is roughly 25–65 microtesla everywhere. A ferrous object perturbs it locally by a tiny amount, so detecting the object means measuring that small change against the large steady baseline.

howItWorks.title: Measuring the field
howItWorks.description: A fluxgate or magnetoresistive magnetometer outputs the field along each axis. Cheap 3-axis modules resolve well under a microtesla — enough to see a car-sized anomaly at short range.

howItWorks.title: Anomaly, not absolute
howItWorks.description: What matters is the deviation from the local baseline. You establish the ambient field, then watch for the perturbation as a ferrous mass comes near — the anomaly is the signal.

howItWorks.title: Gradiometry kills drift
howItWorks.description: The baseline itself wanders with temperature, solar activity, and nearby currents. Two matched sensors a fixed distance apart, subtracted, reject that shared drift and respond only to the steep local gradient of a nearby object.

howItWorks.title: Range and mass
howItWorks.description: The anomaly falls off steeply with distance (roughly as the cube), so detection range depends on the object’s mass and your sensitivity. Understanding that falloff sets realistic expectations for any magnetic sensor.

officialData.whyThisMatters: Long before you can see or hear an approaching person or vehicle, the ground carries their vibration. A geophone — the same sensor used in oil exploration and earthquake monitoring — turns that ground motion into a voltage, and with the right processing you can detect footsteps, tell a person from a vehicle, and estimate direction. This is the principle behind unattended ground sensors used for perimeter monitoring. It is a passive, emission-free build that teaches low- frequency signal detection, simple classification, and the reality of picking a faint signal out of environmental noise. defense signals — a Build List field guide 10 / 17 --- PAGE 11 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand seismic and vibration sensing, very-low-frequency signal conditioning, event detection and simple classification (footstep versus vehicle by frequency and cadence), and sensor siting. Passive ground sensing is used in perimeter security, seismology, and structural monitoring.
officialData.jobMapping: unattended-sensor and perimeter-security engineering — defense sensor, seismic-monitoring, and structural-health teams.
officialData.safety: — a driveway, a fence line, a site perimeter. Keep it on your own property and respect the privacy of anyone nearby; it senses motion, not identity.

howItWorks.title: The geophone
howItWorks.description: A geophone is a coil-and-magnet transducer that outputs a voltage proportional to ground velocity. Footsteps and vehicles couple energy into the ground as low-frequency waves the geophone picks up.

howItWorks.title: The frequency band
howItWorks.description: Seismic events of interest live at low frequencies — footsteps a few to tens of Hz, vehicles lower and more continuous. Amplify and band-pass this range while rejecting wind, mains hum, and higher-frequency noise.

howItWorks.title: Detecting an event
howItWorks.description: A footstep is a short impulsive burst; the detector watches signal energy rise above the background floor and flags an event, much like triggering on a noise-adaptive threshold.

howItWorks.title: Classifying the source
howItWorks.description: A person produces distinct, spaced impulses at a walking cadence; a vehicle produces continuous, lower-frequency energy. Looking at frequency content and rhythm lets you tell them apart — simple classification from a single sensor.

howItWorks.title: Siting and range
howItWorks.description: Coupling to firm ground, sensor depth, and soil type dominate range and sensitivity. Where and how you plant the sensor matters as much as the electronics — the practical heart of unattended sensing.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: El microcontrolador no detecta el módulo o el bus se congela aleatoriamente.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Ausencia de resistencias pull-up adecuadas o cableado demasiado largo con capacitancia parasita > 400 pF.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Añadir resistencias pull-up externas de 2.2 kΩ a 4.7 kΩ entre las líneas SDA/SCL y el riel de 3.3V, y acortar los cables a menos de 10 cm.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicios esporádicos del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al arrancar actuadores o transmisores.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Caída brusca de tensión provocada por el pico de corriente de arranque (inrush current) del periférico.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Soldar un condensador electrolítico de baja ESR de 470 µF a 1000 µF en paralelo con el riel de potencia y alimentar la etapa de potencia mediante una fuente independiente con masa común.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Ruido excesivo o deriva continua en la señal adquirida.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento electromagnético procedente de motores o falta de filtrado cerámico de alta frecuencia en la alimentación.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Colocar un condensador cerámico SMD de 100 nF lo más cerca posible de los pines VDD y GND del sensor, y habilitar un filtro paso bajo digital (DLPF) en el firmware.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Sobrecalentamiento del regulador de voltaje LDO o del circuito integrado.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Disipación de potencia excesiva por caída de tensión elevada (ej. alimentar un chip de 3.3V desde 12V a través de un regulador lineal).
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Reemplazar el LDO lineal por un convertidor reductor conmutado (Buck DC-DC) de alta eficiencia o añadir un disipador de aluminio.

officialData.whyThisMatters: Small drones have gone from novelty to a serious security concern, and detecting them is now a major defense and infrastructure problem. Most drones constantly transmit — a control link on 2.4 or 5.8 GHz and usually a video downlink — and those emissions are a fingerprint you can detect passively with an SDR. Building a drone-detection receiver teaches you to scan the ISM bands, recognise the signatures of drone control and video protocols, and flag a drone’s presence without transmitting anything yourself. It is a receive-only, topical build that sits right at the centre of the fast-growing counter-UAS field. defense signals — a Build List field guide 12 / 17 --- PAGE 13 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand wideband spectrum scanning, recognising signal signatures (frequency-hopping control links, video downlinks), the ISM bands drones use, and energy and feature detection — the passive-sensing core of counter-UAS. It maps directly onto RF-sensing and spectrum- awareness roles.

officialData.safety: — NEVER JAM OR HIJACK This build never transmits. Jamming, hijacking, or spoofing a drone or its GPS is illegal in most countries and can be dangerous, so this stays entirely passive — you sense that a drone is present, nothing more. Respect privacy and spectrum law.

howItWorks.title: Drones are noisy on purpose
howItWorks.description: A drone needs a control link and usually a live video feed, so it is almost always transmitting on 2.4 GHz, 5.8 GHz, or both. Those emissions are exactly what a passive receiver looks for.

howItWorks.title: Scanning the bands
howItWorks.description: An SDR sweeps the ISM bands and builds a spectrogram, or waterfall. Drone control links often frequency-hop across the band in a recognisable pattern, and video downlinks appear as wide, steady carriers.

howItWorks.title: Signatures, not just energy
howItWorks.description: Distinguishing a drone from WiFi and Bluetooth means recognising the shape and timing of its signals — the hopping cadence of the control link, the bandwidth of the video — rather than just seeing energy in the band.

howItWorks.title: Detection and alerting
howItWorks.description: When a matching signature appears, you flag it. Advanced systems classify the drone type from its protocol fingerprint; a first build can simply and reliably say “a drone- like signal is present.”

howItWorks.title: Range and antennas
howItWorks.description: A directional antenna extends range and, swept, hints at direction. Combined with the direction finder from project 2, passive detection can become passive location — all without emitting a thing.

officialData.whyThisMatters: Es el bloque fundamental que diferencia a un aficionado de un ingeniero profesional: control determinista, análisis de tolerancias y fiabilidad en campo.
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand GNSS fundamentals (trilateration from time-of-flight, the role of precise time), NMEA data, why the signal sits below the noise floor and how correlation recovers it, and the concepts of jamming and spoofing resilience. PNT is core defense and aerospace EE.
officialData.jobMapping: positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) engineering — aerospace, defense, autonomous- systems, and timing-infrastructure teams.
officialData.safety: — NEVER JAM OR SPOOF This build only listens. Jamming or spoofing GNSS is a serious federal crime and endangers aircraft, ships, and emergency services, so nothing here transmits and the resilience discussion stays conceptual. Understanding the threat is a defensive skill; creating it is not. defense signals — a Build List field guide 02 / 23 --- PAGE 3 --- ## how it works ▸ Trilateration from time: Each satellite broadcasts its position and an extremely precise time. The receiver measures how long each signal took to arrive, converts that to a distance, and solves for its own position where the ranges intersect — needing at least four satellites to also solve for its own clock error. ▸ Time is the real product: Because position comes from timing, GNSS is first a time system. The satellites carry atomic clocks and the receiver recovers time to nanoseconds — which is why GNSS quietly synchronises power grids, cell networks, and financial systems, and why time itself is a defense priority. ▸ Below the noise floor: The signal arriving at your antenna is weaker than the background noise. The receiver recovers it by correlating against each satellite's known pseudo-random code (a spread-spectrum trick) — a huge processing gain that pulls the signal up out of the noise. ▸ Reading the output: A receiver module outputs standard NMEA sentences over serial: position, altitude, speed, satellites in view, and fix quality. Parsing these is your window into what the receiver is actually doing. ▸ Why it is fragile: The received power is tiny, so a small interferer can jam it, and because the format is public, a fake stronger signal can spoof it. Real systems defend with directional and adaptive antennas, multi-constellation receivers, and spoofing detection — the resilience side of PNT. ## bill of materials COMPONENT PART / SPEC QTY ~COST ELECTRICAL Main Controller ESP32-WROOM-32 Development Board 1 $8.00 GNSS Receiver u-blox NEO-6M GPS Module (GY-NEO6MV2) 1 $12.00 Software Defined Radio RTL-SDR Blog V4 USB Dongle 1 $25.00 PRINTED PARTS & HARDWARE Enclosure Base 3D-printed part 1 $1.50 Enclosure Lid 3D-printed part 1 $0.50 MCU Sled 3D-printed part 1 $0.20 GNSS Module Sled 3D-printed part 1 $0.15 M2.5 Board Screws M2.5x6mm Machine Screws 8 $0.16 M3 Enclosure Screws M3x10mm Socket Head Cap Screws 4 $0.12 M3 Threaded Inserts M3x4mmx5mm Brass Heat-Set Inserts 4 $0.20 Software Defined Radio Mount 3D-printed part 1 $2.00 Build total (as specified) $49.83 ◆ BOM, wiring & render generated in Blueprint — component links via blueprint.am ## wiring at a glance SIGNAL & POWER CONNECTIONS → ESP32 UART2 ↔ NEO-6M — MCU TX2 to GNSS RX, GNSS TX to MCU RX2 → NEO-6M power: 3.3 V + GND from the ESP32 (~100 mA) → Active GPS antenna → NEO-6M, SMA pass-through in the lid → RTL-SDR Blog V4 → host over USB (optional raw-L1 viewing) ## build steps 1 Get a fix Wire the GNSS module to your microcontroller over serial, take it near a window or outside, and wait for a lock. Watch the satellite count climb and the first position fix appear. defense signals — a Build List field guide 03 / 23 --- PAGE 4 --- 2 Parse NMEA Read the NMEA sentences and extract latitude, longitude, altitude, speed, satellites in view, and fix quality. Print them cleanly and confirm they match your real location. 3 Log a track Record position over time and plot it (a walk around the block). See the accuracy, the noise, and how it degrades indoors or under cover. 4 Recover precise time Use the receiver's timing output (the PPS pin, if present) and note how tightly it disciplines time — the feature that makes GNSS a synchronisation backbone. 5 See the raw signal (optional) With an RTL-SDR and an active antenna, tune to L1 (1575.42 MHz) and observe what looks like pure noise — then read how correlation pulls the real signal out. That gap between 'looks like noise' and 'carries the world's timing' is the whole lesson. ## interview questions → How does a GNSS receiver determine its position from satellite signals? → Why does a GNSS fix require at least four satellites, not three? → Why is GNSS fundamentally a timing system? → How is the GNSS signal recovered when it sits below the noise floor? → What is the difference between jamming and spoofing, conceptually? → How do modern receivers improve resilience against interference? ## full wiring schematic signal & power graph — generated in Blueprint · open this build in Blueprint ↗ defense signals — a Build List field guide 04 / 23

officialData.whatThisProves: You understand direction-finding techniques (RSSI / rotational, pseudo-Doppler, and phase-based angle-of-arrival), coherent multi-channel reception, antenna arrays, and the math that turns antenna phase differences into a bearing. Coherent RF and DF are advanced, in-demand skills across SIGINT, EW, and spectrum work.
officialData.jobMapping: signals intelligence, electronic warfare, and spectrum engineering — defense RF, spectrum- monitoring, and search-and-rescue teams.
officialData.safety: , DON'T INTRUDE This is receive-only: you locate transmitters, you never transmit or interfere. Use it for fox-hunting, tracking down interference, or search-and- rescue beacons, and respect privacy and radio law — don't use it to covertly track people. defense signals — a Build List field guide 05 / 23 --- PAGE 6 --- ## how it works ▸ The basic idea: A directional antenna hears a signal loudest when pointed at its source. Rotate it (or steer a phased array electronically) and the direction of peak strength, or of a specific phase relationship, points back toward the transmitter. ▸ RSSI and rotational DF: The simplest method reads received signal strength as you rotate a Yagi; the peak is the bearing. Cheap and intuitive, but reflections and multipath in real environments blur it, which is why better methods exist. ▸ Pseudo-Doppler: Rapidly switching between antennas arranged in a circle imposes a Doppler-like modulation whose phase encodes the arrival angle. It works with a single receiver and is a classic, affordable DF technique. ▸ Phase-based angle-of-arrival: With multiple coherent receivers sharing one clock, you measure the tiny phase difference of the same signal arriving at spaced antennas. That phase difference maps directly to the arrival angle — the method behind precise, modern DF. ▸ From one bearing to a fix: A single bearing is a line; take bearings from two or more locations and where they cross is the transmitter's position. Moving receivers, or multiple stations, turn a direction into a location. BUILD NOTE Start cheap: one RTL-SDR and a directional (Yagi) antenna plus signal strength, or a pseudo-Doppler array. fase2_wiring.busNotes: El bus I2C debe mantenerse con cables de menos de 15 cm para evitar capacitancia parasita excesiva. Si se comparten múltiples sensores, verificar que no haya colisión de direcciones I2C (ej. 0x68 vs 0x69).

mountingNotes: Fijación mecánica rígida: En proyectos de control inercial o sensores de movimiento, fijar la PCB con separadores M2.5 o M3 con arandelas de goma antivibración.
Orientación de los ejes: Alinear el eje X del sensor serigrafiado en la placa con el vector de avance o puntería del dispositivo.
Gestión térmica: Colocar pequeños disipadores autoadhesivos de aluminio en el procesador y chips de potencia si el consumo supera los 500 mW.
Carcasa y blindaje: Diseñar o imprimir en 3D la carcasa en filamento PETG o ABS para resistencia mecánica y térmica en exteriores.

fase4_firmware.loopRate: 250 Hz (4 milisegundos por iteración) sincronizado por interrupción de temporizador
fase4_firmware.algorithm: Arquitectura cíclica determinista con muestreo regularizado por interrupciones de hardware, desacoplando el tiempo de lectura del tiempo de procesamiento y envío.

steps: Paso 1: Test de primer encendido seguro con fuente de laboratorio limitada a 150 mA para proteger contra cortocircuitos accidentales.
Paso 2: Ejecución de un escáner de bus (ej. I2C Scanner) para verificar que el periférico responde en su dirección hex esperada.
Paso 3: Protocolo de reposo estático (Zero-Motion Calibration): Mantener el dispositivo inmóvil sobre una superficie nivelada durante 5 segundos para calcular y restar el sesgo estático (bias).
Paso 4: Validación de rango dinámico: Aplicar estímulos conocidos y verificar mediante el Serial Plotter que la señal responde sin saturación ni ruido espurio.
Paso 5: Calibración de tiempo muerto y seguridad de desconexión (Failsafe timeout): Comprobar que el sistema entra en modo seguro si se interrumpe la comunicación por más de 100 ms.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: El microcontrolador no detecta el módulo o el bus se congela aleatoriamente.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Ausencia de resistencias pull-up adecuadas o cableado demasiado largo con capacitancia parasita > 400 pF.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Añadir resistencias pull-up externas de 2.2 kΩ a 4.7 kΩ entre las líneas SDA/SCL y el riel de 3.3V, y acortar los cables a menos de 10 cm.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicios esporádicos del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al arrancar actuadores o transmisores.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Caída brusca de tensión provocada por el pico de corriente de arranque (inrush current) del periférico.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Soldar un condensador electrolítico de baja ESR de 470 µF a 1000 µF en paralelo con el riel de potencia y alimentar la etapa de potencia mediante una fuente independiente con masa común.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Ruido excesivo o deriva continua en la señal adquirida.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento electromagnético procedente de motores o falta de filtrado cerámico de alta frecuencia en la alimentación.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Colocar un condensador cerámico SMD de 100 nF lo más cerca posible de los pines VDD y GND del sensor, y habilitar un filtro paso bajo digital (DLPF) en el firmware.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Sobrecalentamiento del regulador de voltaje LDO o del circuito integrado.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Disipación de potencia excesiva por caída de tensión elevada (ej. alimentar un chip de 3.3V desde 12V a través de un regulador lineal).
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Reemplazar el LDO lineal por un convertidor reductor conmutado (Buck DC-DC) de alta eficiencia o añadir un disipador de aluminio.

officialData.whatThisProves: You understand magnetometry (fluxgate and magnetoresistive sensors), the Earth's field as a baseline, gradiometry to cancel common-mode drift, calibration, and anomaly detection against a noisy background. Passive magnetic sensing is used across defense, geophysics, and navigation.
officialData.jobMapping: magnetic sensing and geophysical engineering — defense sensor, survey, navigation, and instrumentation teams. ## how it works ▸ The Earth's field as baseline: The geomagnetic field is roughly 25–65 microtesla everywhere. A ferrous object perturbs it locally by a tiny amount, so detecting the object means measuring that small change against the large steady baseline. ▸ Measuring the field: A fluxgate or magnetoresistive magnetometer outputs the field along each axis. Cheap 3-axis modules resolve well under a microtesla — enough to see a car-sized anomaly at short range. defense signals — a Build List field guide 09 / 23

officialData.whyThisMatters: Es el bloque fundamental que diferencia a un aficionado de un ingeniero profesional: control determinista, análisis de tolerancias y fiabilidad en campo.
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand seismic and vibration sensing, very-low-frequency signal conditioning, event detection and simple classification (footstep versus vehicle by frequency and cadence), and sensor siting. Passive ground sensing is used in perimeter security, seismology, and structural monitoring.
officialData.jobMapping: unattended-sensor and perimeter-security engineering — defense sensor, seismic-monitoring, and structural-health teams.
officialData.safety: — a driveway, a fence line, a site perimeter. Keep it on your own property and respect the privacy of anyone nearby; it senses motion, not identity. ## how it works ▸ The geophone: A geophone is a coil-and-magnet transducer that outputs a voltage proportional to ground velocity. Footsteps and vehicles couple energy into the ground as low-frequency waves the geophone picks up. defense signals — a Build List field guide 12 / 23 --- PAGE 13 --- ▸ The frequency band: Seismic events of interest live at low frequencies — footsteps a few to tens of Hz, vehicles lower and more continuous. Amplify and band-pass this range while rejecting wind, mains hum, and higher-frequency noise. ▸ Detecting an event: A footstep is a short impulsive burst; the detector watches signal energy rise above the background floor and flags an event, much like triggering on a noise-adaptive threshold. ▸ Classifying the source: A person produces distinct, spaced impulses at a walking cadence; a vehicle produces continuous, lower-frequency energy. Looking at frequency content and rhythm lets you tell them apart — simple classification from a single sensor. ▸ Siting and range: Coupling to firm ground, sensor depth, and soil type dominate range and sensitivity. Where and how you plant the sensor matters as much as the electronics — the practical heart of unattended sensing. ## bill of materials COMPONENT PART / SPEC QTY ~COST ELECTRICAL Main Microcontroller ESP32-WROOM-32D DevKitC 1 $8.00 Seismic Sensor SM-24 4.5Hz Geophone Element 1 $15.00 High-Gain Amplifier AD623 Instrumentation Amplifier Module 1 $5.00 PRINTED PARTS & HARDWARE Weatherproof Enclosure IP65 Waterproof Junction Box 1 $7.50 Ground Coupling Spike M8 Stainless Steel Threaded Rod 250mm 1 $4.50 Spike Locking Nuts M8 Stainless Steel Hex Nuts 2 $0.30 Geophone Coupler 3D-printed part 1 $0.60 MCU Mounting Sled 3D-printed part 1 $0.25 Amplifier Bracket 3D-printed part 1 $0.15 M3 Board Screws M3x8mm Pan Head Screws 8 $0.40 Build total (as specified) $41.70 ◆ BOM, wiring & render generated in Blueprint — component links via blueprint.am ## wiring at a glance SIGNAL & POWER CONNECTIONS → SM-24 geophone (±) → AD623 IN+ / IN− → AD623 OUT → ESP32 ADC (VP / GPIO36) → AD623 on 3.3 V; REF tied to GND; gain set by RG → Band-pass ~2–50 Hz ahead of the ADC (passive RC or active) → M8 stainless spike couples ground motion into the sealed IP65 box ## build steps 1 Read the geophone Amplify the geophone output and digitize it. Tap the ground nearby and watch the waveform respond — your first ground-motion signal. 2 Condition the band Band-pass to roughly 2–50 Hz to keep footstep and vehicle energy while rejecting wind and mains. Confirm a quiet baseline when nothing is moving. 3 Detect footsteps Compute short-window energy and flag events above a noise-adaptive threshold. Walk toward the sensor and count how far away it first triggers. 4 Classify person vs vehicle Compare the frequency content and rhythm of footsteps versus a rolling vehicle, and build a simple rule that labels each event type. defense signals — a Build List field guide 13 / 23

officialData.whyThisMatters: Es el bloque fundamental que diferencia a un aficionado de un ingeniero profesional: control determinista, análisis de tolerancias y fiabilidad en campo.
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand wideband spectrum scanning, recognising signal signatures (frequency-hopping control links, video downlinks), the ISM bands drones use, and energy and feature detection — the passive-sensing core of counter-UAS. It maps directly onto RF-sensing and spectrum- awareness roles.
officialData.jobMapping: counter-UAS and RF-sensing engineering — drone-defense, critical-infrastructure-protection, and spectrum-monitoring teams.
officialData.safety: — NEVER JAM OR HIJACK This build never transmits. Jamming, hijacking, or spoofing a drone or its GPS is illegal in most countries and can be dangerous, so this stays entirely passive — you sense that a drone is present, nothing more. Respect privacy and spectrum law. defense signals — a Build List field guide 15 / 23 --- PAGE 16 --- ## how it works ▸ Drones are noisy on purpose: A drone needs a control link and usually a live video feed, so it is almost always transmitting on 2.4 GHz, 5.8 GHz, or both. Those emissions are exactly what a passive receiver looks for. ▸ Scanning the bands: An SDR sweeps the ISM bands and builds a spectrogram, or waterfall. Drone control links often frequency-hop across the band in a recognisable pattern, and video downlinks appear as wide, steady carriers. ▸ Signatures, not just energy: Distinguishing a drone from WiFi and Bluetooth means recognising the shape and timing of its signals — the hopping cadence of the control link, the bandwidth of the video — rather than just seeing energy in the band. ▸ Detection and alerting: When a matching signature appears, you flag it. Advanced systems classify the drone type from its protocol fingerprint; a first build can simply and reliably say 'a drone-like signal is present.' ▸ Range and antennas: A directional antenna extends range and, swept, hints at direction. Combined with the direction finder from project 2, passive detection can become passive location — all without emitting a thing. ## bill of materials COMPONENT PART / SPEC QTY ~COST ELECTRICAL Main Processor Raspberry Pi 4 Model B 4GB 1 $55.00 Wideband SDR HackRF One 1 $340.00 Pan Servo Motor MG996R Servo 1 $12.00 Tilt Servo Motor MG996R Servo 1 $12.00 Servo Controller PCA9685 16-Channel PWM Module 1 $7.00 Battery Power Supply Geekworm UPS HAT 1 $35.00 System Status Display 3.5 inch SPI TFT LCD 1 $22.00 PRINTED PARTS & HARDWARE Main Enclosure Base 3D-printed part 1 $3.50 Main Enclosure Lid 3D-printed part 1 $1.50 Raspberry Pi Mount 3D-printed part 1 $0.50 HackRF Mount 3D-printed part 1 $0.75 Status LCD Bezel 3D-printed part 1 $0.30 Pan Servo Bracket 3D-printed part 1 $0.60 Tilt Servo U-Bracket 3D-printed part 1 $0.80 Directional Antenna Platform 3D-printed part 1 $1.20 Pan Thrust Bearing Uxcell F623ZZ Flange Bearing (or similar 40mm Thrust Bearing) 1 $4.50 M3 Machine Screws M3x12mm Socket Head Cap Screws 24 $1.20 M3 Heat-Set Inserts M3x5x4mm Brass Heat Set Inserts 24 $1.92 Servo Controller Mount 3D-printed part 1 $2.00 Build total (as specified) $501.77 ◆ BOM, wiring & render generated in Blueprint — component links via blueprint.am defense signals — a Build List field guide 16 / 23

prepChecklist: Inspeccionar visualmente todos los pines del MCU y módulos para descartar puentes de soldadura.
Verificar con el multímetro en modo continuidad la ausencia total de cortocircuito entre VCC y GND antes de encender.
Comprobar que la tensión de alimentación del riel lógico no exceda el límite del chip (máx 3.6V para ESP32 / Cortex-M).
Tener preparado el cable de datos USB apantallado y el entorno de compilación (Arduino IDE / PlatformIO / Python 3).

Conexión a plano de masa de baja impedancia.
Recepción asíncrona de telemetría / comandos con buffer circular.
Transmisión de configuración hacia el periférico a 115200 baudios.

fase2_wiring.busNotes: Conectar líneas cruzadas (TX del microcontrolador al RX del módulo, y RX al TX). Mantener las masas comunes.

mountingNotes: Fijación mecánica rígida: En proyectos de control inercial o sensores de movimiento, fijar la PCB con separadores M2.5 o M3 con arandelas de goma antivibración.
Orientación de los ejes: Alinear el eje X del sensor serigrafiado en la placa con el vector de avance o puntería del dispositivo.
Gestión térmica: Colocar pequeños disipadores autoadhesivos de aluminio en el procesador y chips de potencia si el consumo supera los 500 mW.
Carcasa y blindaje: Diseñar o imprimir en 3D la carcasa en filamento PETG o ABS para resistencia mecánica y térmica en exteriores.

fase4_firmware.loopRate: 250 Hz (4 milisegundos por iteración) sincronizado por interrupción de temporizador
fase4_firmware.algorithm: Arquitectura cíclica determinista con muestreo regularizado por interrupciones de hardware, desacoplando el tiempo de lectura del tiempo de procesamiento y envío.

steps: Paso 1: Test de primer encendido seguro con fuente de laboratorio limitada a 150 mA para proteger contra cortocircuitos accidentales.
Paso 2: Ejecución de un escáner de bus (ej. I2C Scanner) para verificar que el periférico responde en su dirección hex esperada.
Paso 3: Protocolo de reposo estático (Zero-Motion Calibration): Mantener el dispositivo inmóvil sobre una superficie nivelada durante 5 segundos para calcular y restar el sesgo estático (bias).
Paso 4: Validación de rango dinámico: Aplicar estímulos conocidos y verificar mediante el Serial Plotter que la señal responde sin saturación ni ruido espurio.
Paso 5: Calibración de tiempo muerto y seguridad de desconexión (Failsafe timeout): Comprobar que el sistema entra en modo seguro si se interrumpe la comunicación por más de 100 ms.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: El microcontrolador no detecta el módulo o el bus se congela aleatoriamente.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Ausencia de resistencias pull-up adecuadas o cableado demasiado largo con capacitancia parasita > 400 pF.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Añadir resistencias pull-up externas de 2.2 kΩ a 4.7 kΩ entre las líneas SDA/SCL y el riel de 3.3V, y acortar los cables a menos de 10 cm.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicios esporádicos del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al arrancar actuadores o transmisores.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Caída brusca de tensión provocada por el pico de corriente de arranque (inrush current) del periférico.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Soldar un condensador electrolítico de baja ESR de 470 µF a 1000 µF en paralelo con el riel de potencia y alimentar la etapa de potencia mediante una fuente independiente con masa común.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Ruido excesivo o deriva continua en la señal adquirida.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento electromagnético procedente de motores o falta de filtrado cerámico de alta frecuencia en la alimentación.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Colocar un condensador cerámico SMD de 100 nF lo más cerca posible de los pines VDD y GND del sensor, y habilitar un filtro paso bajo digital (DLPF) en el firmware.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Sobrecalentamiento del regulador de voltaje LDO o del circuito integrado.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Disipación de potencia excesiva por caída de tensión elevada (ej. alimentar un chip de 3.3V desde 12V a través de un regulador lineal).
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Reemplazar el LDO lineal por un convertidor reductor conmutado (Buck DC-DC) de alta eficiencia o añadir un disipador de aluminio.

officialData.whyThisMatters: Every robot, from a vacuum to a Mars rover, runs the same loop: sense the world, decide what to do, act, repeat. A reactive rover is the purest version — an ultrasonic and a pair of IR sensors feed a few simple rules that steer two motors, and the machine roams a room avoiding walls and furniture with no map and no plan. It is the cheapest way to build something that behaves on its own, the payoff is immediate (it just drives off), and it is the chassis and control skeleton every later project in this guide builds on. build robots — a Build List field guide 2 / 15 --- PAGE 3 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand the sense-plan-act loop, distance sensing (ultrasonic time-of-flight, IR reflectance), differential- drive steering, and behavior-based control. That is the foundation of mobile robotics and embedded control.
officialData.jobMapping: mobile robotics & embedded systems — robot-vacuum, warehouse-AMR, and consumer-robotics teams.
officialData.safety: Desconectar hélices y cargas antes del test inicial. Verificar polaridad y limitación de corriente en la fuente.

howItWorks.title: Sense-plan-act
howItWorks.description: The robot reads its sensors, applies a rule to decide a motion, drives the motors, and repeats many times a second. The entire behavior emerges from that tight loop — no global map required.

howItWorks.title: Ultrasonic ranging
howItWorks.description: An HC-SR04 emits a 40 kHz ping and times the echo; distance is the speed of sound times the time, halved. It gives you a “how far to the thing ahead” number tens of times a second.

howItWorks.title: IR reflectance
howItWorks.description: Cheap IR sensors detect a nearby obstacle (or a line or edge) by bounced infrared. Mounted at the corners, they catch what the forward ultrasonic misses.

howItWorks.title: Differential drive
howItWorks.description: Two independently driven wheels (plus a caster) steer by speed difference: equal speeds go straight, unequal speeds turn, opposite spin turns in place. It is the simplest steerable platform there is.

howItWorks.title: Behavior rules
howItWorks.description: A priority list of simple behaviors — if something is close ahead, back up and turn; else if a side sensor fires, veer away; else drive forward — produces surprisingly lifelike wandering. This is behavior-based (subsumption) control.

officialData.whyThisMatters: A robot arm looks simple until you try to move its hand to a specific point in space: you have to solve, in reverse, what every joint angle must be to put the gripper there. That is inverse kinematics, and it is the difference between a servo puppet and a robot you command in coordinates. Build a 4-axis arm, derive its geometry, implement IK, and you can type a position and watch it reach there, then pick up an object and place it somewhere else. It is the classic centrepiece of robotics, the flagship of this guide, and a direct lesson in the math every industrial arm runs. build robots — a Build List field guide 4 / 15 --- PAGE 5 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand forward and inverse kinematics, joint-space versus Cartesian-space control, servo coordination, workspace limits, and trajectory smoothing. Kinematics and manipulation are core to industrial and collaborative robotics.
officialData.jobMapping: robotics and manipulation engineering — industrial-robot, cobot, and automation teams.
officialData.safety: Desconectar hélices y cargas antes del test inicial. Verificar polaridad y limitación de corriente en la fuente.

howItWorks.title: Forward kinematics
howItWorks.description: Given the joint angles and link lengths, trigonometry tells you where the gripper ends up. It is the easy direction, and it is how you verify your model against the real arm.

howItWorks.title: Inverse kinematics
howItWorks.description: Given a target (x, y, z), you solve backward for the joint angles. For a 4-axis arm: base rotation from the target’s bearing, then a planar two-link triangle (shoulder and elbow) solved with the law of cosines, then the wrist to level the gripper.

howItWorks.title: The two-link triangle
howItWorks.description: The shoulder, elbow, and target form a triangle whose sides are your link lengths and the distance to the target. The law of cosines gives the elbow angle; a little more trig gives the shoulder. That is the heart of the solution.

howItWorks.title: Joint limits and workspace
howItWorks.description: Servos only rotate so far and links have fixed lengths, so only a region of space is reachable. Your IK must check reachability and respect limits, or you command the impossible.

howItWorks.title: Smooth motion
howItWorks.description: Jumping servos straight to a new angle is jerky. Interpolating between poses over time (in joint space, or along a straight Cartesian path) makes motion smooth and predictable — the beginning of trajectory planning.

officialBuildSteps.title: Measure and model
officialBuildSteps.description: Measure your link lengths and joint offsets, and write forward kinematics. Command known angles and check the gripper lands where the math predicts.

officialBuildSteps.title: Implement inverse kinematics
officialBuildSteps.description: Solve the base bearing, the two-link triangle with the law of cosines, and the wrist. Command an (x, y, z) and watch the arm reach it. Fix the sign errors — there will be some.

officialBuildSteps.title: Add limits and smoothing
officialBuildSteps.description: Reject unreachable targets, clamp joint limits, and interpolate between poses so moves are smooth. Trace a straight line and a circle in the air.

officialBuildSteps.title: Pick and place
officialBuildSteps.description: Add the gripper, command a sequence — move above an object, descend, grip, lift, move, release — and place objects from one spot to another. Film it from the side.

officialData.whyThisMatters: Nothing stops a scroll like a small four-legged robot walking across a table. Each leg is a little robot arm with its own inverse kinematics, and walking is the art of moving them in a coordinated rhythm — a gait — while keeping the body balanced over the feet still on the ground. Build a 12-servo quadruped, solve leg IK, and implement a creep or trot gait, and you have a machine that walks, turns, and stands up on its own. It is the most ambitious build in this guide, a genuine mechatronics and control challenge, and the same fundamentals behind every legged robot from research labs to robot dogs. build robots — a Build List field guide 7 / 15
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand leg inverse kinematics, gait generation and phasing, static stability (support polygons), servo torque budgeting, and coordinating many actuators in real time. Legged locomotion is one of the most demanding — and most exciting — corners of robotics.
officialData.jobMapping: legged robotics and mechatronics — robot-dog, humanoid, and research-lab robotics teams.
officialData.safety: Desconectar hélices y cargas antes del test inicial. Verificar polaridad y limitación de corriente en la fuente.

howItWorks.title: BUILD NOTE Print a proven open-source quadruped frame rather than designing your own, use decent metal-gear servos (cheap plastic ones strip under load), and power the servos from a dedicated high-current supply. Get one leg’s IK working standing still before you attempt a single step. Legs are arms
howItWorks.description: Each leg has three joints — hip abduction, hip pitch, knee — and placing a foot at an (x, y, z) is the same inverse-kinematics problem as the arm, solved twelve times over for four legs.

howItWorks.title: Gaits
howItWorks.description: A gait is the pattern of which legs are in the air and which are on the ground. A creep moves one leg at a time (slow, always stable); a trot moves diagonal pairs together (faster, needs balance). Phasing the legs correctly is what makes walking work.

howItWorks.title: Stability
howItWorks.description: When a leg lifts, the body must stay balanced over the remaining feet. The support polygon — the area under the grounded feet — must contain the centre of mass, or the robot tips. Shifting the body before lifting a leg is the trick.

howItWorks.title: Swing and stance
howItWorks.description: A stepping leg swings forward through the air; the grounded legs stroke backward together to push the body forward. Coordinating swing and stance across all legs, cycle after cycle, is the gait engine.

howItWorks.title: Torque and timing
howItWorks.description: Twelve servos moving under load draw serious current and must move smoothly and in sync. A dedicated supply, sensible speeds, and a fixed-rate control loop are the difference between a walk and a twitching heap.

officialData.whyThisMatters: A robot that can see is a robot that can do almost anything, and the simplest vision task — find a thing and follow it — teaches the whole perception-to-action pipeline. Put a camera on your rover or a pan-tilt head, detect a coloured object (or a face) with OpenCV, and steer the robot to keep it centred and at a set distance. The result follows you around a room, and the pipeline (capture, detect, compute error, control) is exactly what robot vacuums, delivery robots, and industrial vision systems run. It is the bridge from blind reactive behavior to robots that understand what is in front of them. build robots — a Build List field guide 9 / 15
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand image capture and processing, object detection (colour segmentation, face and feature detection), turning detection into a control error, visual servoing, and the latency and robustness issues of real-world vision. Perception plus control is the core of modern robotics.
officialData.jobMapping: robot perception and computer-vision engineering — autonomous-vehicle, delivery-robot, and industrial-vision teams.
officialData.safety: Desconectar hélices y cargas antes del test inicial. Verificar polaridad y limitación de corriente en la fuente.

howItWorks.title: Capture and detect
howItWorks.description: A camera grabs frames; OpenCV finds the target — simplest via colour segmentation (threshold in HSV for a coloured ball), or a face or feature detector. The output is a bounding box or centroid in pixel coordinates.

howItWorks.title: From pixels to error
howItWorks.description: The target’s horizontal offset from image centre is your steering error; its apparent size is your range error. Perception has become two numbers a controller can use.

howItWorks.title: Visual servoing
howItWorks.description: Feed those errors into control loops: turn toward the target to zero the horizontal error, drive forward or back to hold the size at a setpoint. The robot now tracks and follows — a control loop closed through a camera.

howItWorks.title: Latency and robustness
howItWorks.description: Vision is slow and noisy compared to a sensor: frames take time, detection jitters, lighting changes ruin colour thresholds. Filtering the detection and tuning gains for the latency are what make tracking smooth.

howItWorks.title: Stepping up
howItWorks.description: Swap colour segmentation for a lightweight neural detector (a MobileNet-class model on a Pi) and the same pipeline tracks people or objects by class — the path to real-world perception.

steps: Paso 1: Test de primer encendido seguro con fuente de laboratorio limitada a 150 mA para proteger contra cortocircuitos accidentales.
Paso 2: Ejecución de un escáner de bus (ej. I2C Scanner) para verificar que el periférico responde en su dirección hex esperada.
Paso 3: Protocolo de reposo estático (Zero-Motion Calibration): Mantener el dispositivo inmóvil sobre una superficie nivelada durante 5 segundos para calcular y restar el sesgo estático (bias).
Paso 4: Validación de rango dinámico: Aplicar estímulos conocidos y verificar mediante el Serial Plotter que la señal responde sin saturación ni ruido espurio.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: El microcontrolador no detecta el módulo o el bus se congela aleatoriamente.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Ausencia de resistencias pull-up adecuadas o cableado demasiado largo con capacitancia parasita > 400 pF.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Añadir resistencias pull-up externas de 2.2 kΩ a 4.7 kΩ entre las líneas SDA/SCL y el riel de 3.3V, y acortar los cables a menos de 10 cm.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicios esporádicos del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al arrancar actuadores o transmisores.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Caída brusca de tensión provocada por el pico de corriente de arranque (inrush current) del periférico.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Soldar un condensador electrolítico de baja ESR de 470 µF a 1000 µF en paralelo con el riel de potencia y alimentar la etapa de potencia mediante una fuente independiente con masa común.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Ruido excesivo o deriva continua en la señal adquirida.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento electromagnético procedente de motores o falta de filtrado cerámico de alta frecuencia en la alimentación.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Colocar un condensador cerámico SMD de 100 nF lo más cerca posible de los pines VDD y GND del sensor, y habilitar un filtro paso bajo digital (DLPF) en el firmware.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Sobrecalentamiento del regulador de voltaje LDO o del circuito integrado.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Disipación de potencia excesiva por caída de tensión elevada (ej. alimentar un chip de 3.3V desde 12V a través de un regulador lineal).
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Reemplazar el LDO lineal por un convertidor reductor conmutado (Buck DC-DC) de alta eficiencia o añadir un disipador de aluminio.

officialData.whyThisMatters: A gripper that only knows its finger position will crush a strawberry and drop a coffee cup. Give it a sense of touch — a force sensor in the fingertip and a control loop on grip force — and it can pick up an egg, a paper cup, or a tool with just the right squeeze. Building one teaches force sensing, compliant mechanisms, and force control as opposed to position control, which is the difference between industrial pick-and-place and robots that can handle the messy, fragile real world. It is a compact, satisfying build with an unforgettable demo. build robots — a Build List field guide 11 / 15
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand tactile and force sensing (FSRs, load cells), compliant gripper design, closed-loop force control versus position control, grasp detection, and the mechanics of gentle manipulation — core to manipulation and soft- robotics engineering.

howItWorks.title: BUILD NOTE A servo-driven parallel or fin-ray (compliant) gripper printed from an open design is enough. Put the force sensor in a fingertip pad, and remember the sensor reads a squeeze, not a mass — you are controlling grip force, not measuring weight. Sensing touch
howItWorks.description: A force-sensitive resistor (FSR) drops in resistance as you press it; a load cell flexes and changes a strain-gauge bridge. Either gives you a voltage that rises with grip force at the fingertip.

howItWorks.title: Position vs force control
howItWorks.description: A position-controlled gripper closes to a set opening regardless of what is in it — fine for rigid parts, disastrous for fragile ones. Force control closes until the fingertip force reaches a setpoint, then holds, adapting to any object.

howItWorks.title: Compliance helps
howItWorks.description: Flexible fingers (fin-ray or soft pads) conform to an object’s shape, spreading contact and forgiving errors. Mechanical compliance does half the work before the control loop even acts.

howItWorks.title: Grasp detection
howItWorks.description: A rising force signal tells you contact happened; a stable force tells you the grasp is secure; a sudden drop tells you the object slipped. Reading these events is how a robot knows what its hand is doing.

howItWorks.title: The control loop
howItWorks.description: Command the servo to close, read fingertip force, and stop (or servo around) at the target force. Set a low target for an egg, a higher one for a tool — the same gripper, different objects.

officialData.whyThisMatters: The rover in project 1 wanders blind; this one knows where it is. Put a spinning LiDAR on a wheeled base, add wheel odometry, and run SLAM — simultaneous localisation and mapping — and the robot builds a map of the room as it drives while tracking its own position inside it. Then give it a goal and it plans a path around the furniture and drives there. This is the technology in every robot vacuum and warehouse robot, and building it end to end is the capstone of this guide: perception, estimation, mapping, and planning in one machine. build robots — a Build List field guide 13 / 15
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand odometry and its drift, LiDAR scanning, SLAM at a conceptual and practical level (scan matching, pose estimation, occupancy grids), and path planning on a real robot — the complete autonomy stack of mobile robotics, and one of the most in-demand skill sets in the field.
officialData.jobMapping: autonomous-navigation and SLAM engineering — robot-vacuum, warehouse-AMR, delivery-robot, and autonomy teams.
officialData.safety: Desconectar hélices y cargas antes del test inicial. Verificar polaridad y limitación de corriente en la fuente.

howItWorks.title: BUILD NOTE Use the tooling
howItWorks.description: a Raspberry Pi running ROS 2 with a cheap 2D LiDAR (RPLidar A1 or LD19) and the slam_toolbox and Nav2 packages gets you a working map and navigation without writing SLAM from scratch. Learn what the packages do first; go deeper on the algorithms once it drives. Odometry, and why it drifts: Counting wheel rotations gives you a position estimate, but wheel slip and small errors accumulate, so odometry alone wanders off within metres. It is a good short-term guess and a bad long-term truth.

howItWorks.title: LiDAR scans the room
howItWorks.description: A spinning 2D LiDAR returns hundreds of range measurements per revolution — a slice of the surrounding walls. Each scan is a snapshot of what the world looks like from where the robot is.

howItWorks.title: SLAM
howItWorks.description: scan matching: SLAM compares each new scan to the map so far, finds the pose that best aligns them, corrects the odometry drift, and adds the scan to the map. Localisation and mapping improve each other — the “simultaneous” in SLAM.

howItWorks.title: The occupancy grid
howItWorks.description: The map is a grid where each cell is free, occupied, or unknown, built up from the scans. That grid is what the planner reasons over.

howItWorks.title: Planning and navigation
howItWorks.description: Given the map and a goal, a planner (A* over a costmap that inflates obstacles) finds a path, and a local controller drives it while dodging anything new. The robot is now autonomous in a space it built its own model of.

officialData.whyThisMatters: Every piece of defense electronics has to survive an environment full of interference — radar, lightning, hostile transmitters, and the electromagnetic pulse that hardened systems are built to shrug off. The defense against all of it is the same physics: a conductive enclosure that stops fields at the boundary. Build a Faraday cage, put a phone inside and watch it lose signal, then measure exactly how many decibels of attenuation your seams, mesh, and gaskets buy you with an SDR. It is a beginner build with an unforgettable demo, and it teaches EMC and hardening — the survivability discipline that sits under every ruggedised system. survive the field — a Build List field guide 2 / 16 --- PAGE 3 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand electromagnetic shielding (skin depth, aperture leakage, seam and gasket design), how to measure attenuation in dB with a source and a receiver, and the difference between shielding, filtering, and grounding — the fundamentals of EMC and hardening engineering.
officialData.jobMapping: EMC, EMI, and hardening / survivability engineering — defense electronics, aerospace, and ruggedised-systems teams.
officialData.safety: Desconectar hélices y cargas antes del test inicial. Verificar polaridad y limitación de corriente en la fuente.

howItWorks.title: SP01 · 22.4 °C · ε 0.95 Fields stop at a conductor
howItWorks.description: A conductive shell redistributes charge and induces currents that cancel an external field inside. At radio frequencies a thin conductive layer is enough — the field only penetrates to the “skin depth,” microns at GHz.

howItWorks.title: Apertures leak
howItWorks.description: Shielding fails at holes and seams, not through the metal. Any gap longer than a fraction of the wavelength acts as a slot antenna and lets the field in — which is why gaskets, overlapping seams, and fine mesh matter more than thick walls.

howItWorks.title: Measuring attenuation
howItWorks.description: Put a known signal outside (WiFi, a broadcast station, a small legal ISM transmitter) and measure inside with an SDR. The drop, in dB, is your shielding effectiveness — and every 20 dB is a tenfold reduction in field strength.

howItWorks.title: EMP and lightning
howItWorks.description: A nuclear EMP or a nearby lightning strike is a fast, enormous field pulse. Hardened systems combine a shielded enclosure with filtered entry points and surge protection, because the shield is only as good as its weakest cable.

howItWorks.title: Shield, filter, ground
howItWorks.description: A complete hardening strategy layers three things: shield the enclosure, filter every wire that crosses it, and manage the grounding so currents flow around the electronics rather than through them.

fase2_wiring.busNotes: Conectar líneas cruzadas (TX del microcontrolador al RX del módulo, y RX al TX). Mantener las masas comunes.

mountingNotes: Fijación mecánica rígida: En proyectos de control inercial o sensores de movimiento, fijar la PCB con separadores M2.5 o M3 con arandelas de goma antivibración.
Orientación de los ejes: Alinear el eje X del sensor serigrafiado en la placa con el vector de avance o puntería del dispositivo.
Gestión térmica: Colocar pequeños disipadores autoadhesivos de aluminio en el procesador y chips de potencia si el consumo supera los 500 mW.
Carcasa y blindaje: Diseñar o imprimir en 3D la carcasa en filamento PETG o ABS para resistencia mecánica y térmica en exteriores.

fase4_firmware.algorithm: Arquitectura cíclica determinista con muestreo regularizado por interrupciones de hardware, desacoplando el tiempo de lectura del tiempo de procesamiento y envío.

steps: Paso 1: Test de primer encendido seguro con fuente de laboratorio limitada a 150 mA para proteger contra cortocircuitos accidentales.
Paso 2: Ejecución de un escáner de bus (ej. I2C Scanner) para verificar que el periférico responde en su dirección hex esperada.
Paso 3: Protocolo de reposo estático (Zero-Motion Calibration): Mantener el dispositivo inmóvil sobre una superficie nivelada durante 5 segundos para calcular y restar el sesgo estático (bias).
Paso 4: Validación de rango dinámico: Aplicar estímulos conocidos y verificar mediante el Serial Plotter que la señal responde sin saturación ni ruido espurio.
Paso 5: Calibración de tiempo muerto y seguridad de desconexión (Failsafe timeout): Comprobar que el sistema entra en modo seguro si se interrumpe la comunicación por más de 100 ms.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: El microcontrolador no detecta el módulo o el bus se congela aleatoriamente.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Ausencia de resistencias pull-up adecuadas o cableado demasiado largo con capacitancia parasita > 400 pF.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Añadir resistencias pull-up externas de 2.2 kΩ a 4.7 kΩ entre las líneas SDA/SCL y el riel de 3.3V, y acortar los cables a menos de 10 cm.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicios esporádicos del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al arrancar actuadores o transmisores.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Caída brusca de tensión provocada por el pico de corriente de arranque (inrush current) del periférico.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Soldar un condensador electrolítico de baja ESR de 470 µF a 1000 µF en paralelo con el riel de potencia y alimentar la etapa de potencia mediante una fuente independiente con masa común.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Ruido excesivo o deriva continua en la señal adquirida.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento electromagnético procedente de motores o falta de filtrado cerámico de alta frecuencia en la alimentación.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Colocar un condensador cerámico SMD de 100 nF lo más cerca posible de los pines VDD y GND del sensor, y habilitar un filtro paso bajo digital (DLPF) en el firmware.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Sobrecalentamiento del regulador de voltaje LDO o del circuito integrado.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Disipación de potencia excesiva por caída de tensión elevada (ej. alimentar un chip de 3.3V desde 12V a través de un regulador lineal).
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Reemplazar el LDO lineal por un convertidor reductor conmutado (Buck DC-DC) de alta eficiencia o añadir un disipador de aluminio.

officialData.whyThisMatters: Every aircraft, drone, and glider in the defense world was shaped in a wind tunnel long before it flew, and you can build a real one on a desk. A fan, a settling chamber, a honeycomb flow straightener, a smooth contraction, and a clear test section give you steady laminar air; add a smoke wand and the streamlines over a 3D-printed wing become visible, and a load cell turns the invisible force of lift into a number you can plot against angle of attack. It is the flagship of this guide — a genuine aerospace instrument, visually spectacular, and a hands-on route into aerodynamics and aircraft design. survive the field — a Build List field guide 4 / 16 --- PAGE 5 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand subsonic aerodynamics (lift, drag, angle of attack, stall), flow conditioning (honeycombs, screens, contraction ratio), flow visualisation, and force measurement with a balance. That is the core of aerospace and aerodynamics engineering, and the wind-tunnel workflow every aircraft program uses.

howItWorks.title: SP02 · 27.9 °C · ε 0.95 Lift from pressure
howItWorks.description: Air moving over a curved wing speeds up and its pressure drops relative to the underside; the pressure difference integrates into lift. Angle the wing up and lift grows — until the flow separates and the wing stalls.

howItWorks.title: Conditioning the flow
howItWorks.description: A fan produces swirl and turbulence. A settling chamber slows the air, a honeycomb straightens it, fine screens break up turbulence, and a contraction (a smooth nozzle) accelerates it into a clean, uniform test-section flow.

howItWorks.title: Seeing the flow
howItWorks.description: A thin stream of smoke (or fog from a small glycol fogger) introduced upstream follows the streamlines, making the flow over the wing visible — attached flow, the stagnation point, and the separated wake at stall.

howItWorks.title: Measuring force
howItWorks.description: Mount the wing on a sting connected to a load cell (or two, for lift and drag). As the fan runs, the load cell reads the aerodynamic force directly; plot lift against angle of attack to see the lift slope and the stall.

howItWorks.title: Reynolds number
howItWorks.description: The key scaling parameter for aerodynamics. Your small, slow tunnel runs at low Reynolds number, which changes stall behaviour and lift coefficients — so you report airspeed, chord, and Re with every result.

officialData.whyThisMatters: Helmets, vehicle panels, and protective gear are built from composites engineered to absorb impact — and the way engineers develop them is by making test panels and hitting them, repeatably, with an instrumented impactor. Lay up your own panels from carbon, fiberglass, and aramid with different stacks and resins, then build a drop tower that drops a known mass from a known height onto them while an accelerometer records the impact. Compare the panels: which cracked, which delaminated, which shrugged it off. It is hands-on materials engineering with a dramatic slow-motion payoff, and it is exactly how protective structures get designed. survive the field — a Build List field guide 7 / 16
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand composite layup (fiber types, weave, stacking sequence, resin), energy absorption and failure modes (delamination, fiber breakage), instrumented impact testing, and turning a test into data. Materials and structural-test engineering underpin every protective system in defense.
officialData.jobMapping: materials and protective-structures engineering — composites, structural-test, and protective- equipment teams.
officialData.safety: , NOT BULLETS This is a drop-weight impact test, the standard lab method — and it stays that way. Never test panels with firearms or projectiles: it is illegal outside a licensed range, extremely dangerous, and not what this build is for. Wear eye protection, keep hands clear of the drop path, and handle composites with gloves and a respirator — epoxy and fiber dust are real hazards. SP03 · 31.6 °C · ε 0.95

fase2_wiring.busNotes: Conectar líneas cruzadas (TX del microcontrolador al RX del módulo, y RX al TX). Mantener las masas comunes.

mountingNotes: Fijación mecánica rígida: En proyectos de control inercial o sensores de movimiento, fijar la PCB con separadores M2.5 o M3 con arandelas de goma antivibración.
Orientación de los ejes: Alinear el eje X del sensor serigrafiado en la placa con el vector de avance o puntería del dispositivo.

steps: Paso 1: Test de primer encendido seguro con fuente de laboratorio limitada a 150 mA para proteger contra cortocircuitos accidentales.
Paso 2: Ejecución de un escáner de bus (ej. I2C Scanner) para verificar que el periférico responde en su dirección hex esperada.
Paso 3: Protocolo de reposo estático (Zero-Motion Calibration): Mantener el dispositivo inmóvil sobre una superficie nivelada durante 5 segundos para calcular y restar el sesgo estático (bias).
Paso 4: Validación de rango dinámico: Aplicar estímulos conocidos y verificar mediante el Serial Plotter que la señal responde sin saturación ni ruido espurio.
Paso 5: Calibración de tiempo muerto y seguridad de desconexión (Failsafe timeout): Comprobar que el sistema entra en modo seguro si se interrumpe la comunicación por más de 100 ms.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: El microcontrolador no detecta el módulo o el bus se congela aleatoriamente.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Ausencia de resistencias pull-up adecuadas o cableado demasiado largo con capacitancia parasita > 400 pF.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Añadir resistencias pull-up externas de 2.2 kΩ a 4.7 kΩ entre las líneas SDA/SCL y el riel de 3.3V, y acortar los cables a menos de 10 cm.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicios esporádicos del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al arrancar actuadores o transmisores.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Caída brusca de tensión provocada por el pico de corriente de arranque (inrush current) del periférico.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Soldar un condensador electrolítico de baja ESR de 470 µF a 1000 µF en paralelo con el riel de potencia y alimentar la etapa de potencia mediante una fuente independiente con masa común.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Ruido excesivo o deriva continua en la señal adquirida.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento electromagnético procedente de motores o falta de filtrado cerámico de alta frecuencia en la alimentación.
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Colocar un condensador cerámico SMD de 100 nF lo más cerca posible de los pines VDD y GND del sensor, y habilitar un filtro paso bajo digital (DLPF) en el firmware.

fase6_troubleshooting.symptom: Sobrecalentamiento del regulador de voltaje LDO o del circuito integrado.
fase6_troubleshooting.cause: Disipación de potencia excesiva por caída de tensión elevada (ej. alimentar un chip de 3.3V desde 12V a través de un regulador lineal).
fase6_troubleshooting.fix: Reemplazar el LDO lineal por un convertidor reductor conmutado (Buck DC-DC) de alta eficiencia o añadir un disipador de aluminio.

officialData.whyThisMatters: Sound travels farther and faster in water than radio ever could, which is why navies listen. Build a hydrophone from a piezo element potted in epoxy, drop it in a lake, and you hear propellers, outboards, and the whole underwater soundscape; add a second hydrophone a known distance away, measure the time difference of arrival, and you get the bearing to the source — passive sonar, the technique behind anti-submarine warfare and marine monitoring. It is receive-only, cross-disciplinary (acoustics, transducers, signal processing), and a strikingly different sensing domain from the RF work in the rest of the series. survive the field — a Build List field guide 10 / 16 --- PAGE 11 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand underwater acoustics, piezo transducers and potting, low-noise preamplification, time-difference-of- arrival bearing estimation, and cross-correlation. Passive acoustic sensing is core to naval, marine, and monitoring engineering.
officialData.jobMapping: naval acoustics and underwater-sensing engineering — sonar, marine-monitoring, and ocean- engineering teams.
officialData.safety: , DON'T DISTURB This is receive-only. Never build an active (transmitting) sonar — loud underwater sound harms marine life and is regulated. Keep clear of swimmers and boat traffic, don’t leave gear in the water, and respect wildlife. You are listening, nothing more.

howItWorks.title: SP04 · 18.2 °C · ε 0.95 Sound in water
howItWorks.description: Water carries sound at about 1,500 m/s — four times faster than air — with far less loss, so a boat’s propeller can be heard kilometres away. That efficiency is why sonar, not radar, sees underwater.

howItWorks.title: The hydrophone
howItWorks.description: A piezoelectric element turns pressure waves into voltage. Potting it in epoxy (or oil-filling a rubber housing) waterproofs it while coupling sound in; a low-noise preamp right at the element lifts the tiny signal before the cable adds noise.

howItWorks.title: Listening
howItWorks.description: Feed the preamp into an audio interface and you hear the underwater world — engines, rain, fish, wakes. A spectrogram shows the tonals of a propeller (its blade-rate lines) that identify a vessel.

howItWorks.title: Bearing from two ears
howItWorks.description: Two hydrophones a known distance apart receive the same sound at slightly different times. That time difference of arrival, measured by cross-correlating the two channels, gives the angle the sound came from — the same trick your ears use.

howItWorks.title: Ambiguity and range
howItWorks.description: Two hydrophones give a bearing with a left / right ambiguity; three resolve it; moving or multiple stations can triangulate range. Real towed arrays are just many hydrophones doing this at scale.

officialData.whyThisMatters: Getting supplies to a precise spot from the air is a logistics problem the defense world solved with self-steering parafoils: a ram-air canopy with servo-pulled control lines and a GPS-guided controller that flies the payload to a coordinate. Build a small one — a ram-air kite canopy, two servos on the brake lines, a GPS and IMU on the payload box — drop it from a legal height, and watch it turn toward the landing point and flare. It is aerospace, control, and embedded engineering in one build, it is pure cargo delivery, and it is one of the most satisfying autonomous systems you can make. survive the field — a Build List field guide 12 / 16 --- PAGE 13 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand ram-air parafoil aerodynamics and control (brake-line steering), guidance to a waypoint from GPS and heading, closed-loop heading control under wind, and the
officialData.jobMapping: aerial-delivery, small-UAS, and guidance-navigation-control engineering — logistics-systems and unmanned-aerial teams.
officialData.safety: , AND SAFELY This carries supplies and nothing else — it is a delivery system and stays one. Drop only in a clear, open area you have permission to use, never over people, buildings, or roads; keep the payload small and soft; follow your local drone and airspace rules for whatever lifts it. A self-steering canopy is still a falling object.

howItWorks.title: SP05 · 36.4 °C · ε 0.95 The ram-air canopy
howItWorks.description: A parafoil is a soft wing — cells inflated by ram air — that glides, so it can be steered. Pull the left brake line and the left side slows and dips, turning the canopy left; pull both to flare and slow the descent.

howItWorks.title: Servo steering
howItWorks.description: Two small servos on the payload box shorten the left and right brake lines. That gives a controller a heading command — the whole point that makes the drop precise rather than wherever the wind takes it.

howItWorks.title: Knowing where you are
howItWorks.description: GPS gives position; a magnetometer and IMU give heading. The controller computes the bearing to the landing point and the heading error.

howItWorks.title: Closing the loop
howItWorks.description: A heading controller steers toward the landing point, correcting for wind drift, and manages the glide so it arrives high enough to turn into the wind and flare on the final approach — the same logic full-scale systems use.

howItWorks.title: The drop platform and safety
howItWorks.description: The payload is lifted by a drone, a kite, or a safe high point, released to deploy the canopy, then flies itself down. Everything about the test — area, altitude, payload mass — is chosen so a failure lands harmlessly.

officialData.whyThisMatters: Outdoors, GPS tells the flight controller where the drone is. Indoors there is no GPS, and a drone drifts like a balloon in a draft. The fix is the same trick an optical mouse uses: a tiny downward camera (a PMW3901 optical-flow sensor) watches the floor texture slide by and reports velocity, while a rangefinder gives height. Feed both to the flight controller and it holds position — a hover you can let go of, indoors, that stays put. It is the cheapest, most dramatic upgrade there is, and it is the foundation for every kind of indoor autonomy. drone upgrades — a Build List field guide 2 / 16 --- PAGE 3 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand optical flow (velocity from image motion), why flow must be scaled by height, how a flight controller’s estimator fuses a new sensor, and how to configure and validate that fusion safely. That is the core of GPS-denied navigation.
officialData.jobMapping: drone autonomy and GNC engineering — indoor-drone, inspection, and navigation teams.

howItWorks.title: UPGRADE 01 · REV A Optical flow
howItWorks.description: The sensor sees floor texture move across its tiny image and reports pixel displacement per frame — the angular rate of the ground beneath. It is a mouse sensor pointed at the floor from a metre up.

howItWorks.title: Height turns flow into velocity
howItWorks.description: The same angular rate means a faster ground speed when you are higher, so the flight controller needs the height from a rangefinder (a ToF like the VL53L1X or a TFmini) to scale flow into linear velocity.

howItWorks.title: Fusion in the estimator
howItWorks.description: The flight controller’s EKF fuses flow velocity with the IMU and the rangefinder into a position estimate whose drift is bounded by the flow — no GPS required. It also enables terrain-following altitude hold.

howItWorks.title: Light and texture
howItWorks.description: Flow needs texture and light: a blank floor or a dim room starves it. A small downward LED and a textured surface make the difference between a locked hover and a drift.

howItWorks.title: Flight modes
howItWorks.description: With flow enabled, position-hold and loiter modes work indoors, and the controller arbitrates between GPS and flow depending on what is healthy. Understanding that arbitration is what keeps a hybrid indoor / outdoor flight safe.

prepChecklist: Inspeccionar visualmente todos los pines del MCU y módulos para descartar puentes de soldadura.
Verificar con el multímetro en modo continuidad la ausencia total de cortocircuito entre VCC y GND antes de encender.
Comprobar que la tensión de alimentación del riel lógico no exceda el límite del chip (máx 3.6V para ESP32 / Cortex-M).
Tener preparado el cable de datos USB apantallado y el entorno de compilación (Arduino IDE / PlatformIO / Python 3).
